A1.name: Beginner
A1.canDo: Introduce yourself, order food, ask simple questions about prices and times.
A1.exampleGloss: My name is Sam and I live in Cologne.

A2.name: Elementary
A2.canDo: Talk about your day and your past weekend, make appointments, write short messages.
A2.exampleGloss: At the weekend I went to the cinema with friends.

B1.name: Intermediate
B1.canDo: Handle everyday situations on your own, give reasons and opinions, write personal and simple formal emails.
B1.exampleGloss: I could not come because I had to work longer.

B2.name: Upper intermediate
B2.canDo: Discuss abstract topics, argue for and against, write clear formal complaints and applications.
B2.exampleGloss: Although the rent has gone up, I would like to keep the flat.

C1.name: Advanced
C1.canDo: Follow demanding texts and talks, argue a position with nuance, write well-structured essays, reports and formal statements.
C1.exampleGloss: In view of rising rents, many are demanding that housing construction be speeded up.

C2.name: Mastery
C2.canDo: Understand practically everything you read or hear, weigh up arguments from several sources, and express fine shades of meaning in any register, from a formal objection to a review.
C2.exampleGloss: Scarcely had the compromise been announced when it was already being called into question again by the very members who had negotiated it.

a1-cafe-invite.title: A message to a friend
a1-cafe-invite.prompt: Write a short message to your friend Lena: you are at the café "Lindenblatt". Ask if she wants to come, say until when you are there, and what you are drinking.

a1-hotel-form.title: An email to a hotel
a1-hotel-form.prompt: Write a short email to the Hotel Seeblick: you want a single room for two nights from Friday. Ask for the price and if breakfast is included.

a2-birthday.title: A birthday invitation
a2-birthday.prompt: Write a short email to a friend: invite them to your birthday party on Saturday. Say when it starts, where it is, and what they should bring. 30-40 words.

a2-sick-course.title: Missing a course
a2-sick-course.prompt: Write to your teacher, Herr Klein: you are ill and cannot come to the German course tomorrow. Say what you have, and ask what the homework is. 30-40 words.

a2-new-flat.title: Your new flat
a2-new-flat.prompt: Write to your friend Jonas: you have a new flat. Describe it, say what you like about it, and invite him to visit.

b1-missed-party.title: Sorry I missed your party
b1-missed-party.prompt: Write an email (about 80 words) to a friend: you missed their party last weekend. Apologise, explain why you could not come, and suggest a new meeting.

b1-teacher-absent.title: An email to your teacher
b1-teacher-absent.prompt: Write a formal email (about 40 words) to your German teacher, Frau Weber: you cannot attend the next lesson. Give the reason and ask for the homework.

b1-forum-homeoffice.title: A forum post: working from home
b1-forum-homeoffice.prompt: Write a forum post (about 80 words): is working from home a good idea? Give your opinion, one advantage, one disadvantage, and an example from your life.

b2-course-complaint.title: A complaint to a language school
b2-course-complaint.prompt: Write a formal complaint (about 150 words) to a language school: your course had no teacher for three sessions. Describe what happened, say what you expect the school to do, and set a deadline for their answer.

b2-application.title: An application for an internship
b2-application.prompt: Write a formal application (about 150 words) for an internship at a museum in Hamburg: say why you are interested, what experience you have, and when you are available.

c1-letter-to-editor.title: A letter to the editor on the four-day week
c1-letter-to-editor.prompt: A newspaper has published an article claiming that a four-day week would harm the economy. Write a letter to the editor (about 200 words): refer to the article, take a clear position with two arguments, address one counter-argument, and end with a recommendation or an appeal.
points: a recommendation or an appeal at the end

c1-statement-management.title: A statement to management on working from home
c1-statement-management.prompt: Your company wants to end working from home completely. As the spokesperson of your team, write a formal statement to the management (about 220 words): describe the current arrangement, explain the consequences of the plan for the team, propose a compromise, and ask for a meeting.

c2-objection-bank-fees.title: An objection to a bank about unlawful account fees
c2-objection-bank-fees.prompt: Your bank raised its account fees two years ago without your explicit consent and now refuses to refund them, citing your "tacit acceptance". Write a formal objection to the bank (about 260 words): set out the facts with dates and amounts, state the legal basis and the ruling you rely on, demand the refund with a deadline, and announce the steps you will take if the bank does not comply.
points: the facts with dates and amounts
the legal basis and the ruling you rely on
the demand for a refund with a deadline

c2-expert-statement-council.title: An expert statement to the city council on a car-free centre
